data.narrative:
Cresilon, a Series B biotech company founded by Joe Landolina, has raised $113M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public companies in the Biotech & Health sector, with private comparables including Eikon Therapeutics, Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and New Limit at Series B/C stages.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression anchors to Cresilon's $113M total raised and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $215M. The peer-median method examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $539M (Eikon Therapeutics, Series B) to $10.3B (Colossal Biosciences, Series C), producing a median of $3.5B. Public-comp anchoring via EV/Sales multiples (9.2x median across RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures. The wide spread between methods reflects stage and outcome heterogeneity within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $182M (low) to $4.0B (high), with a median of $1.8B. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, clinical-stage risk, and whether peer valuations reflect comparable capital efficiency or product maturity. Stage-progression yields the most conservative estimate; peer medians anchor toward higher valuation but exhibit substantial dispersion.
